svg.title: Dog-Ear reading assistant, camera highlights and barcode books: architecture
svg.desc: The reader's browser runs the Dog-Ear web app: assistant panel, tool runner, voice, camera capture and barcode scanner. Supabase hosts two Edge Functions that hold the Anthropic API key and check the reader's token and quota, plus Postgres with Row Level Security. Anthropic's API runs Claude Opus 5.5 for the assistant and for reading the cropped passage. Public web APIs supply word definitions and book details by ISBN.
svg.text: Reading assistant, camera highlights and barcode books
RFC 0002 · Architecture. Claude decides what to do; every change runs in the browser, as the reader, so Row Level Security still applies.

g.text: tool calls and results
verify token, quota, key
as the reader
You type or speak to the assistant panel.
Speech becomes text in the browser.
The panel sends your message, and each tool
result, with your sign-in token (JWT).
The function checks the token and today's quota,
adds the API key and calls Claude.
Claude's reply, or a tool call, streams back
through the function to the panel.
The browser runs each tool through useBookData,
as you, so Row Level Security applies.
The reply appears in the chat and, if you like,
is read aloud.
The cropped passage goes to read-passage; Claude
reads its text back into the highlight form.
A scanned ISBN is looked up in Open Library or
Google Books; create_book adds the book.
Word lookups use the dictionary cache first,
then dictionaryapi.dev and Datamuse.
